passage: Hemant let go of his father's hand for one second to look at a kite, and when he looked up the bazaar was all strangers' legs. His heart thudded. He closed his eyes. "Where was I holding his hand? The sweet shop with the jalebi pans. And the blue gate next to it." He reasoned that Papa would look back along the way they had come, and the sweet shop was the one place they both knew. So he walked, not ran, past two stalls, stopped by the blue gate and stood still. Sunaina Aunty from the sweet shop noticed and handed him a stool. Soon his father's checked shirt came through the crowd.

qa.q: Which two landmarks did Hemant remember?
qa.a: He remembered the sweet shop and the blue gate.

qa.q: What was Hemant thinking as he closed his eyes to recall the way?
qa.a: He was calming himself and working out where he had last held his father's hand.

qa.q: What else could Hemant do if his father does not come soon, and why?
qa.a: He could ask Sunaina Aunty to phone his father, because a shop owner at a fixed spot is an easy, safe helper.

qa.q: How might Hemant's father look for him?
qa.a: His father would probably retrace their steps too, going to where they were last together, so the landmark gives them a good chance to meet.

grounding: A boy recalls the landmarks near where he last held his father's hand and calmly returns to them.
